settings.ekit_heading_title: Nil T2 Filing in Mississauga for Dormant and Numbered Corporations
settings.ekit_heading_extra_title:
Plenty of Mississauga corporations spend a year doing nothing at all. The company was set up for a venture that never started, or it traded once and went quiet, or it exists only to hold a name. None of that removes the return. The Canada Revenue Agency expects a T2 for the year regardless, and the only thing that ends the requirement is dissolving the corporation.

That is the whole of what this service does. We take the corporation number and the year end, confirm the year really was nil, prepare the return, send a T183CORP for signature and transmit it. Whether the registered office is in Meadowvale, Port Credit or a home address off Hurontario, the work is the same and happens entirely online.

A nil T2 does not cover your Ontario annual return through the Ontario Business Registry. We tell you if you still owe one.

A federal Corporations Canada annual return costs $12.00 and is due within 60 days of your anniversary. It is a government fee and HST does not apply to it.

This service is for a corporation with no activity in the tax year. A corporation with investment income, rental income, or dividends paid or received is not nil. If your corporation is not nil, we move your file to gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus applicable sales tax per year and tell you before any further charge.

settings.title: Mississauga Nil T2 Filing: Questions We Are Asked

settings.html:
Is a Mississauga corporation that never started trading still required to file?

Yes. The requirement follows the corporation, not the trading. A company incorporated for a venture that never began still files a T2 for each tax year it exists. Numbered corporation filing.

How do I know my year was actually nil?

Nothing came in and nothing went out: no sales, no expenses claimed, no movement through the bank account, nobody on payroll. If any of those is untrue the year is not nil, and we say so before charging anything. What no activity means.

What is my filing date?

Six months after your own fiscal year end, not a fixed date in the calendar. A September 30 year end means a March 31 filing date. Work out your date.

Four years are outstanding. Where do I start?

At the oldest one. Each year is its own return and its own $300.00 plus HST, filed in sequence so the CRA account reconciles year by year. Catch-up filing.

What am I signing, and can I do it from my phone?

A T183CORP, one per tax year, which authorises the electronic transmission. It is signed on screen, on any device, and nothing is printed. How signing works.

Is my Ontario annual return part of this?

No, and the two are often confused. The annual return is filed with the Ontario Business Registry and is a separate obligation from the T2. We check whether yours is outstanding and tell you. Check your date.

The corporation holds a rental property. Does it qualify?

No. Rent received is income, so the year is not nil whatever the profit was. The same applies to interest, dividends received or dividends paid out. Holding corporations.

I have moved abroad. Can the filing still go ahead?

Yes. Signing is electronic, so a director can authorise the return from any country. Non-resident owned corporations.

We are winding the company up. Is a final return needed?

Yes, and it is what closes the file. A final T2 runs to the dissolution date and is due six months after it. Final T2 before dissolution.

Does a dormant company really have to keep filing every year?

Every year, until it is dissolved. A year that is skipped does not fall away; it stays outstanding on the CRA account until the return is transmitted. The full answer.
